item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q020_syntaxin_fragment_reclassification","answer":"In current SCOPe release 2.08, the partial structures d1br0a_ and d1ez3a_/d1ez3b_/d1ez3c_, together with full-domain chain d1dn1b_, all have SCCS a.47.2.1: all-alpha class (a), STAT-like fold (a.47), t-SNARE superfamily (a.47.2), and t-SNARE family (a.47.2.1). The sequence records make the coverage difference explicit: 1br0 A and 1ez3 A contain 120 and 124 residues, respectively, whereas 1dn1 B contains 222 residues. Thus, the early fragment assignments should now be interpreted as partial observations of a fold subsequently corroborated in the complete syntaxin domain—not as evidence that those fragments are autonomous biological domains or suitable whole-domain representatives.\n\nMembership in the same family provides strong evidence that these syntaxin fragments and the full domain are homologous t-SNARE proteins. It does not justify transferring complete domain boundaries, interaction surfaces, conformational behavior, or detailed function from a fragment. Nor does placement in the broader STAT-like fold alone establish homology or functional equivalence to other STAT-like proteins. For local modeling, 1br0 or 1ez3 can be templates only for their covered regions; full-domain modeling and representative selection should use a complete syntaxin structure. Current SCOPe places d1dn1b_ under an “automated matches” protein grouping, while retaining the same family classification; 1dn1 itself is obsolete and replaced by 3c98, so its classification remains informative but current coordinates should come from the replacement when appropriate. Finally, only 1dn1 chain B is syntaxin: chain A is separately classified as e.25.1.1 and must not inherit the syntaxin/t-SNARE annotation.","evidence_used":["/api/v1/","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1br0","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1ez3","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1dn1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1br0/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1ez3/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1dn1/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1br0/chains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1ez3/chains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1dn1/chains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1br0a_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1ez3a_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1dn1b_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1dn1a_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/17772","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/17768","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/302344","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47664","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/311131","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47663","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/191190","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47662","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47661","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47660","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/47654","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/46456","/api/v1/sequences/sids/d1br0a_?release=2.08","/api/v1/sequences/sids/d1ez3a_?release=2.08","/api/v1/sequences/sids/d1dn1b_?release=2.08","/api/v1/releases","/api/v1/releases/1.55/pdb/1dn1/domains","/api/v1/releases/1.57/pdb/1dn1/domains","/api/v1/releases/1.59/pdb/1dn1/domains","/api/v1/releases/1.61/pdb/1dn1/domains","/api/v1/releases/1.63/pdb/1dn1/domains","/api/v1/releases/1.65/pdb/1dn1/domains","/api/v1/releases/1.67/pdb/1dn1/domains","/api/v1/releases/1.69/pdb/1dn1/domains","/api/v1/releases/1.71/pdb/1dn1/domains","/api/v1/releases/1.73/pdb/1dn1/domains","/api/v1/releases/1.75/pdb/1dn1/domains","/api/v1/releases/1.55/sids/d1dn1b_","/api/v1/releases/1.55/sids/d1br0a_","/api/v1/releases/1.55/sids/d1ez3a_"]}]}
